title: manifest.v1: the plugin manifest, 'csl-plugin-manifest/1'
description: The manifest a plugin's developer signs. It is the ten fields of 'csl-plugin-manifest/vNext' (core/recursion_core/plugin_security/manifest.py) with the same meanings, plus three: runtime (how the plugin's code is run), interface (which plugin API it is written against) and files (every file of the package with its SHA-256, so the signature covers the whole package and not only the entry file). The manifest is read as bytes in the restricted canonical form (ASCII, sorted keys, whole numbers, no spaces) and the developer's Ed25519 signature is over those bytes. PROVISIONAL (recommended, not decided): that this contract is frozen as version 1 now, and the five permission names after 'order'. Four rules the parser enforces cannot be written in a schema and are listed in README.md: permissions must be in the order this schema lists them; network_destinations and credential_refs must be sorted; files must contain the entry file, with the digest artifact_sha256 names; and the bytes must be in canonical form. Permissions are only ever appended to the list: an existing name never changes its place or its meaning, so the signed bytes for an existing set of permissions never change.

plugin_id.description: 2 to 64 characters: a lower-case letter, then lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' or '-'. 'host' is the core's own name and no plugin may claim it.

developer_key.description: The developer's Ed25519 public key: 64 lower-case hex digits.

permissions.description: What the plugin asks for. The first seven are today's. The last five are new with version 1 and PROVISIONAL, names and order both: surface (it adds themes and layouts; never the approval area), command (it adds commands), subscribe (it is given events), tool (it declares tools), run (it starts runs it owns).

credential_refs.description: Names of credentials the plugin asks to use. A name, never a credential.

runtime.description: How the plugin's code is run. 'python-sandboxed/1': Python run in a sandboxed host process outside the daemon, behind the wall of the system it runs on; a plugin author writes the same plugin.py as before, and only the place it runs changes. 'python-inprocess/1' retires: in every 1.0.x release a manifest that names it is read as if it named 'python-sandboxed/1' (the plugin runs in a sandboxed host, never in the daemon) and the developer sees the finding 'runtime_inprocess_retiring'; from 1.1.0 on it is refused 'runtime_retired'. Any other value is refused at install and at load, and nothing is run; a name held for a later release (#/$defs/reserved) is refused with its own text. Runtimes are only ever appended to this list: a later runtime arrives as a new name, under unchanged plugins.

interface.description: The plugin API the package is written against.

files.description: Every file of the package: its path inside the package (forward slashes; no segment starts with a dot, so no '.', no '..' and no absolute path) and its SHA-256.

reserved.description: Names held for a later release. A manifest that uses one is refused, typed, with that name's own text, and nothing is run. The parser refuses them; this schema refuses them by the list of allowed values of the field they would go in ('enum' at '/runtime', or at '/permissions/N' for a permission). Every list here is only ever appended to, and reserved is not frozen: a reserved name may be corrected until the first build that answers it.

runtime.description: Runtime names held for a later release. The parser refuses each with the code 'runtime_reserved'.

wasm-component/1.description: A WebAssembly component whose interface is generated from the same message schema as the plugin protocol. Refused with: 'wasm-component/1 is reserved for a later release; this release runs python-sandboxed/1 only.'

data/1.description: A package that holds only data, such as a theme, and starts no interpreter. Refused with: 'data/1 is reserved; not run in this release.'

permission.description: Permission names held for a later release. The parser refuses each with the code 'permission_reserved' and the words 'reserved; not available in this release'. None is in the list of permissions, and nothing grants one.

schedule.description: To start runs on a schedule or on an event.

memory.description: To keep and read what a persistent agent remembers between runs.

computer.description: To use a computer or a browser on the user's behalf.

record_kind.description: Record kinds held for a later release. This manifest has no field that declares record kinds, so none is refused here yet; the names are held so that no plugin claims one first.

trigger.v1.description: What starts a scheduled or event-driven run.

agent.v1.description: A persistent agent: its name, its instructions and what it may do.

memory.lesson.v1.description: One lesson a persistent agent keeps between runs.

work.packet.v1.description: A unit of work handed from one node to another.

node.v1.description: A machine that takes part in running work.

permission.description: In canonical order. A manifest and a grant list permissions in this order.
